newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Apr 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Apr 17.

text.p: There are 75 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

The MING PAO DAILY said the government's plan to move the right of abode bill on June 30 was a pity, a move that put political considerations above the interests of the people. The government and the post-handover administration should put aside their political differences and work for the general good of the community, the paper said.

The Beijing-backed WEN WEI PO accused the British Hong Kong authorities of trying to create a legal vacuum in the right of abode matter. The government was sacrificing the right of travel of Hong Kong people and the interests of emigrants in a move to damage Hong Kong's interests, it said.

The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said the Sino-British Land Commission was not an unqualified success. After July when the new government takes over responsibility for land allocation, it will be free to respond according to market requirements so greater sanity should prevail. The first act of the new administration must be to utilise resources so that prices can settle at a realistic level, the paper said.
